items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: I wasn't acquainted with Miss Senegal... So I went out to Miss Senegal and I visited her and I told her that I could help her along that line... I finally taught them the steps and taught them the whole thing. And made it possible for her to produce that choir trail.

ctx.x: Professor Minetta's told us about those. He played at the tuxedo dance hall and some of the houses and all too. Yes. Yes. He's told us all about that. But I used to play for private people.

Private dancers I used to play. And I had a whole set of... a whole set of dances. During those ten days, they used to have a certain order of dances, you see? They start off with a waltz, you see? Then they did a polka, you see? Then a mizooka, then a shardis. They used to dance those kind of dances before and then come back to a polka and repeat that. And then they would have a waltz and quadrille. And when the waltz was danced, as the rule, the dancers used to get their partner for the quadrille to make sure…
I heard about it. You organized the group for the Creole Festival? I organized the group for the quadrille. Now I'm going to tell you how that happened.
